mbm-2001.clue: The little blue fish always wins.
mbm-2001.quote: There's a fish painted on the floor of our pool. I race it on the way out and give it a head start on the way back. I've yet to see it out of breath.

mbm-2002.clue: I put the coldest seat on the warmest quilt.
mbm-2002.quote: Dad drove the early bus. I pieced its blue seats into a blanket and added one square of orange for the spot where the heater worked. He put his feet straight there.

mbm-2003.clue: Our mute button is a woolly hat.
mbm-2003.quote: The guitarist kept stepping on his tuner in the quiet verse. I put my bright green hat over it at rehearsal. He played a perfect set and went home wearing the hat.

mbm-2004.clue: My chalk bag has two tiny windows.
mbm-2004.quote: I made it look like a cabin because my climbing partner calls the halfway ledge home. We stop there for a breath and he knocks on my little cabin before we carry on.

mbm-2005.clue: I quilted the seats before I quilted the audience.
mbm-2005.quote: When the old hall came down I kept a strip of red curtain. I cut tiny red theatre seats across my quilt and let my cousins embroider themselves in the row.

mbm-2006.clue: The blurry dog is the only one I'd print twice.
mbm-2006.quote: I was taking a long exposure of our garden gate. The dog ran through and turned into a silver streak. My sister can still identify him by the one floppy ear at the end.

mbm-2007.clue: My dance card is also a recipe.
mbm-2007.quote: The cook wrote the soup ingredients on the back of my dance card. We waltzed through three songs and went home to make the soup. I can still hum it while I chop.

mbm-2008.clue: I can fit a bridge into a single stroke.
mbm-2008.quote: At low tide my kayak passes the old stone bridge just as its arch joins the reflection. I pause with the paddle flat. For a second I'm sitting inside a ring.

mbm-2009.clue: I've got a jacket for lending pencils.
mbm-2009.quote: I sew a row of tiny pencil loops inside my old denim jacket. At art nights I open it like a tool chest and everyone chooses a color. The yellow one always comes home shorter.

mbm-2010.clue: I painted the shadow before the boat.
mbm-2010.quote: My uncle wanted a picture of his dinghy, but the rain kept him ashore. I painted its blue shadow on the slipway. When the sun came out he put the boat where I'd drawn it.

mbm-2011.clue: The ogre came home in a teabag box.
mbm-2011.quote: My little cousin built a cardboard house for a fantasy card I traded him. It has a teabag for a doormat and a pencil drawing of our kitchen. The ogre looks very comfortable.

mbm-2012.clue: I save the softest clave for the last verse.
mbm-2012.quote: My uncle and I play son outside his workshop. When the neighbors turn on the porch lights, I swap my bright new claves for his worn pair. The last verse belongs to the street.

mbm-2013.quote: At the airfield a little plane disappeared behind one cloud just as I finished its wing in my sketch. I left the patch blank. My dad says it's the best drawing I've made of how high it was.

mbm-2014.clue: There's always one dry sock at breakfast.
mbm-2014.quote: A tent leak found my bag. I hung our socks in a ring around a sunny stump while we ate. My sister rotated the stump display like a shopkeeper till everybody got one warm foot.

mbm-2015.clue: I named one hold for a supermarket shelf.
mbm-2015.quote: After weeks missing a high climbing hold, I reached for the last cereal box at home and felt the same stretch. Now my climbing partner gives me a thumbs-up and whispers cornflakes when I get close.

mbm-2016.clue: I put the puddle in the corner for a reason.
mbm-2016.quote: I quilted my first pair of boots from brown canvas scraps. The lower seam sits in a blue patch. Dad said he'd spent enough time drying the originals for that to be accurate.

mbm-2017.clue: I paint the moth when the fan is folded.
mbm-2017.quote: I put one wingtip on the outside rib and the rest across the folds. Open it at the right speed and the little green moth seems to settle on your palm.

mbm-2018.clue: We take our first dance at the bus shelter.
mbm-2018.quote: When the club doors are still shut we practice a few steps in the shelter window. In winter our breath fogs over our reflections and we have to finish the turn by ear.

mbm-2019.clue: I photograph empty seats after everyone leaves.
mbm-2019.quote: After family lunch the chairs tell you who sat where. A jacket on one, a little ribbon on another, and Dad's seat turned toward the window. That picture went in our album beside the group shot.

mbm-2020.clue: That pocket was big enough for a whole school.
mbm-2020.quote: When the old classroom curtains became quilt scraps, my mother gave me a pocketful of chalk ends. I stitched one little white line across each green square like an unfinished sum.

mbm-2021.clue: I put the quiet colors round the edges.
mbm-2021.quote: My nephew chose all the brightest scraps for his blanket. When he fell asleep in the armchair, I added a border the same pale blue as his closed eyelids in the window light.

mbm-2022.clue: We made a flag for the nicest miss.
mbm-2022.quote: My disc landed in the creek and floated past our picnic like a little red boat. My aunt tied a paper flag to a stick at the point where we rescued it. That's our new turnaround spot.

mbm-2023.clue: I bought the key for the sound it made.
mbm-2023.quote: I collect old keys from the market. One rings a clear high note when I tap it against my cup. I don't know what opens its lock, but it opens every tune on my breakfast table.

mbm-2024.clue: We gave the dragon a day off.
mbm-2024.quote: The little dragon in our game wore its cardboard feet down to stubs. My cousin made it a chair and played its turns as a messenger pigeon. The dragon spent Sunday ruling from a matchbox throne.

mbm-2025.clue: I choose thread by the color of the rain.
mbm-2025.quote: The first quilt I made for my sister was all gray scraps. We sat by the window matching them to a shower, from silver on the glass to charcoal under the sill. She's never called it a dull quilt.
